content.text: prolactinoma: cabergoline = tx of choice (better tolerated and more potent than bromocriptine); stop it at a positive preg test if trying to conceive; acromegaly: cabergoline is typically used in mild dz.
high doses (esp cabergoline) are thought to have caused valvular heart dz in PD; consider echo surveillance, esp > 3 mg/wk; may cause ↑impulsivity and occasionally psychosis.
Start 0.25 mg PO twice weekly. Titrate by ↑ 0.25 mg twice weekly at intervals of no less than 4 wks to achieve normal serum prolactin. Max 1 mg twice weekly.

CI: uncontrolled hypertension; known hypersensitivity to ergot derivatives. CI: Hx of cardiac valvular disorders (valvulopathy of any valve shown on pre-tx evaluation, incl echocardiography) or pericardial fibrosis; Hx of pleural, pulmonary, or retroperitoneal fibrotic disorders. B4 initiating, evaluate for valvular heart disease, incl w/ an echocardiogram; if valvular disease is detected, ⍉ administer. Monitor for valvulopathy w/ a cardiac echocardiogram at intervals of 6 to 12 mo or as clinically indicated. If pleural, pericardial, retroperitoneal, or pulmonary fibrosis occur, discontinue. Check BP at baseline and during tx and monitor for orthostatic hypotension; warn pts about the risk and precautions when rising from a supine or sitting position. Specifically ask pts about new or increased gambling urges, sexual urges, uncontrolled spending, or other urges; consider dose reduction or stopping if such urges develop. ⍉ use for inhibition or suppression of postpartum physiologic lactation (risk of serious adverse reactions). Not recommended w/ D2-antagonists such as phenothiazines, butyrophenones, thioxanthenes, or metoclopramide. Severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh C) not recommended; in moderate HI (Child-Pugh B) increase monitoring of cabergoline-associated adverse reactions. OD: take measures to support BP if necessary.
